source.title: Scaling description of generalization with number of parameters in deep learning
source.authors: M. Geiger; Arthur Jacot; Stefano Spigler; Franck Gabriel; Levent Sagun; Stéphane d'Ascoli; G. Biroli; Clément Hongler; M. Wyart

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps network size and measures test error, directly testing model-wise generalization as capacity changes.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports a cusp-like test-error maximum near the jamming transition for its MNIST fully connected networks, followed by a slow decrease. It also reports a nearly flat ensemble test-error curve above the transition. Other size-sweep curves appear in figures without a textual description of their shape. The paper does not report a test-error sweep over epochs or sample sizes, and its references to other studies' results are not extracted as findings here.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps parameter count for fully connected MNIST networks and CIFAR10 CNNs and reports test error. It finds a cusp at the jamming (interpolation) threshold, then a slow decrease. It also uses ensembles to probe whether the second descent is driven by variance. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors attribute the improvement with N past N* to output fluctuations from NTK initialization decaying as N^−1/4, giving test error ε_N−ε_∞ ∼ N^−1/2. They attribute the cusp at N* to a divergence of the output norm when no regularization is used. They conclude that ensembling several networks just beyond N* is best for a given compute budget.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses parameter-count sweeps and test error, but its settings include MNIST parity classification on PCA components and CIFAR10 CNNs, with its own training choices and ensemble comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome differs for the MNIST ensemble curve, which is nearly flat above N*, versus the single-network MNIST curve. The study also presents results for early stopping and for a CIFAR10 CNN, but the text does not describe those curves' shapes.

fits_no_version.finding: The output norm ||f_N|| diverges as (N−N*)^−1 at jamming without regularization. Finite training times cut off the divergence (Fig 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The test-error cusp at the interpolation threshold is caused by divergence of the output-function norm in unregularized training.

fits_no_version.finding: The gap between a single network's test error and the ensemble's scales as N^−1/2 (Fig 6D). Output fluctuations scale as N^−1/4 (Fig 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Past the threshold, test error decays to a plateau as a power law N^−1/2 set by NTK initialization fluctuations.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: Several size-dependent results are available only as plotted curves, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The fully connected MNIST experiment uses parity classification on only the first 10 PCA components; the paper's evidence is limited to its tested datasets and architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the tested version were left out.

untested.parts: Only small fully connected nets (MNIST parity, 10 PCA inputs) and one vanilla CNN on CIFAR10 were tested. For the CNN, the shape below the transition is not described in the text.
No label-noise sweep, no multiple peaks, and no tuned explicit regularization. The early-stopping effect on the test-error peak is shown only in a figure.

missing.what: Output variance ||f_N−f̄_N||² peaks at the jamming transition and then decays as N grows
CIFAR10 single-network and ensemble accuracies are given in the text (about 67–72%, about 77.5%, about 80.5–80.7%)
After ensembling, N slightly above N* generalizes slightly better than N≫N*

record.verdict_notes: V6 support is indirect: variance is reduced by ensembling rather than by noise or regularization sweeps. The CNN uses linear-hinge loss with SGD; the FC networks use square-hinge loss with full-batch Adam.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-size behavior for its fully connected MNIST setup and reports additional size-sweep results for CIFAR10 CNNs; it does not establish the claim for deep networks generally.
No test-error curve over training epochs is reported.
No sweep varying the number of training samples near the interpolation threshold is reported.
The empirical tests use deep neural networks, not a range of model classes.
The paper does not test whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.

The study does not vary label noise or compare peaks under optimally tuned regularization. Its discussion of unregularized training and early stopping does not test the stated noise/regularization dependence.
The study does not re-express the curve against an effective number of parameters to test whether it becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: fully-connected networks
rows.operation_detail: Sweep network parameter count and measure test error after training.

conditions.value: classify 10k training images by parity using their first 10 PCA components

rows.value: A cusp-like local maximum near N*=825, then a slow decrease as N grows; fitted asymptotic plateau ε∞=0.054.
rows.note: The paper also gives a fitted asymptotic form εN−ε∞=B0 N−1/2+B1 N−3/4, with B0=6.4 and B1=−49.

rows.subject: fully-connected networks, ensemble average f̄N
rows.operation_detail: Sweep network parameter count and measure test error of an ensemble average over independent initializations.

conditions.value: classify 10k training images by parity using their first 10 PCA components

rows.baseline: average single-network test error is shown for comparison; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: Nearly flat test error for N>N*.
rows.note: This is the ensemble curve, not the single-network result; the paper says ensemble averaging with n=20 makes test error nearly flat above N*.
rows.check: For V1 the second descent is absent: ensemble test error is nearly flat above N*. For V6 the row supports the variance account: removing initialization variance removes the improvement with N. Section 7 adds that the ensemble is slightly better just above N* than at N≫N*.

source_check.correct: Absent for V1's post-threshold descent; observed for the tested variance-dependence component of V6. These version-specific states require separate assignments.
source_check.problem: The shared absent state fits V1 but misstates the evidence supporting V6.

rows.subject: fully-connected networks with early stopping
rows.operation_detail: Plot test error across parameter counts for the early-stopping condition.

conditions.value: classify 10k training images by parity using their first 10 PCA components

rows.note: The early-stopping curve is plotted, but the text does not describe its size-dependent shape.
rows.check: The early-stopping curve is shown only in the figure. Its relevance to V6 (peak vs regularization) cannot be read from the text.

rows.subject: CNN (vanilla model with 3 convolutional and 1 fully-connected layers)
rows.size_stated: filter count f varied from 2^1 to 2^11; total parameter counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Sweep filter count and plot test error after training.

conditions.value: 10-class image classification; 50,000 training and 10,000 test images

rows.note: The figure plots average test error versus filter count, but the text does not explicitly describe the shape of this curve.
rows.check: The value is not figure-only. The text gives mean accuracy of about 67–72% just past the transition (f≈40–64), rising to just under 77.5% for the widest models. That is a second descent after the transition. The rise of error toward the transition is not described in the text.

source_check.correct: Section 8 states mean accuracy approximately 67–72% at f approximately 40, 48, 64, and slightly below 77.5% for the widest models. These accuracy values establish post-transition improvement; numerical test-error values and a transition peak are not explicitly stated.
source_check.locator_found: Section 8, paragraph preceding Figure 8; Figure 8 caption.
source_check.problem: The result is not exclusively figure-only: the prose supplies accuracy values.

rows.subject: CNN ensemble average f̄N
rows.size_stated: filter count f varied from 2^1 to 2^11; total parameter counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Sweep filter count and plot test error for an ensemble average over independent initializations.

conditions.value: 10-class image classification; 50,000 training and 10,000 test images

rows.baseline: average single-network test error is shown for comparison; numerical baseline not stated
rows.note: The text reports ensemble performance and its maximum as accuracy, but does not explicitly state the shape of the ensemble test-error curve.
rows.check: The value is in the text: ensemble accuracy is about 80.5–80.7% just past the transition and peaks at f=64. The ensemble does not improve further with width, so there is no continued second descent.

source_check.correct: Ensemble accuracy is approximately 80.5–80.7% soon after the transition; peak ensemble accuracy is approximately 80.7% at f=64. Continued improvement with increasing width is absent.
source_check.problem: The ensemble result and its optimum are stated numerically in the prose as accuracy.

relationships.condition: Ensemble averages of 20 independently initialized networks (MNIST FC and CIFAR10 CNN)
relationships.reason: Ensemble test error is flat or best just above N* rather than falling with size, so the second descent depends on initialization variance (r2, r5).

relationships.reason: Ensembling removes the improvement above N*, and output variance peaks at jamming (Fig 5, not in rows). Both fit a variance-driven peak (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Output variance peaked at jamming, and ensembling removed the generalization improvement above N*.

statements.correction: MNIST: parity classification using ten PCA components, 10,000 training images and 50,000 test images. CIFAR10: ten-class classification using 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images. MNIST ensemble error nearly flat above N*; CIFAR10 ensemble accuracy maximal at f=64.
statements.problem: The conditions describe reduced MNIST/CIFAR tasks, but this study's CIFAR10 experiment uses the standard full dataset and all ten classes.
